transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Poor drying on a Bosch WTN85201GB is most often caused by restricted airflow rather than a broken part. This model is a condenser dryer, so it relies heavily on clean filters to move air through the system. The two most common causes are:
1. A clogged lint filter or condenser: If these are blocked with fluff, the machine cannot circulate hot air effectively, leaving clothes damp even after hours.
2. Laundry entering too wet: If your washing machine didn't spin well (or you used a low-spin programme), the dryer has to work much harder and may not finish in two hours. Please try these checks:
1. Clean the lint filter located inside the door frame. Remove it, wash off all fluff under warm water, and let it dry before refitting.
2. Open the small flap at the bottom left of the front panel to access the condenser unit. Pull it out carefully (it may be heavy with water), rinse it thoroughly under the tap until the water runs clear, shake out excess water, and let it drip-dry completely before sliding it back in.
3. Ensure you are not overloading the drum (keep it to about two-thirds full) and that your washing machine is spinning at a high speed (e.g.If these steps don't resolve the issue, please let me know if the air coming out of the vent feels hot during operation.

Did the filter and the condenser. Door filter had fluff and a waxy film, and water barely went through until I scrubbed it. The condenser had never been cleaned and the front was matted with lint, but it rinsed clean with the shower head. Load is normal and the spin is 1200. It's a condenser so there's no vent, just warm damp air in the room.

We need to determine if the machine is actually generating heat. Please run a standard cotton drying programme for 10–15 minutes. With the appliance switched on, carefully place your hand near the door seal (do not touch hot parts) to feel if the air inside is getting warm or hot. Is it heating up now, or does it still feel just like room-temperature air? If it feels cold or only slightly warm after 15 minutes, the heater element has likely failed or a thermal safety cut-out has tripped (often caused by the previous blockages). If it is getting quite hot but clothes are still damp, we may have an airflow issue inside the cabinet or a sensor fault.
Yes, it's hot inside the drum after 20 min, so it is heating. Also the water container only gets a little water after a cycle.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The next most likely cause on this Bosch model is that the moisture sensors inside the drum are dirty. These dryers use metal strips to detect when clothes are dry; if they are coated in fabric conditioner residue or fluff, the machine thinks the load is dry much sooner than it actually is and stops prematurely. Please look for two or three metal strips near the lint filter housing inside the drum. Wipe them clean with a damp cloth and a little white vinegar to remove any coating, then try a drying cycle again. If they were already clean (or cleaning them doesn't help), we need to check if air is actually moving through the machine properly. Please let me know what you find.

Wiped the sensor bars with vinegar, they were slightly dull. I also vacuumed fluff out of the slot behind the condenser housing. Ran a test cycle after all the cleaning and the clothes dried in about 100 minutes with the container nearly full.

That is excellent news. The fact that the clothes dried in 100 minutes and the water container filled up suggests that the machine is now working correctly. The issue was a combination of restricted airflow (the blocked condenser and lint filter) and dirty moisture sensors. When the filters were clogged, the dryer couldn't circulate air properly, and when the sensor bars were coated in residue, the machine didn't know the clothes needed more time. Cleaning both resolved it. To keep it running well:
• Clean the lint filter before every cycle.
• Rinse the condenser unit once a month or whenever you notice the drying taking longer than usual.
• Wipe the sensor bars with vinegar occasionally to prevent residue buildup. You should be good to go. If this happens again despite regular cleaning, let me know.
